title: Cartesian descent charts for compatible local immersions
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For each point $i$ choose an open neighbourhood $U_i$ containing $i$, a scheme $W_i$, and an immersion $j_i:W_i\to U_i$. Assume compatibility: for every scheme $T$, points $i,k$, and maps $a:T\to U_i$, $b:T\to U_k$ with equal composites to $S$, the map $a$ factors through $j_i$ if and only if $b$ factors through $j_k$. Then there exist a scheme $Z$ and a morphism $q:Z\to S$ such that for each $i$ there is a morphism $e_i:W_i\to Z$ making the square with top map $j_i$, left map $e_i$, right map $U_i\to S$, and bottom map $q$ Cartesian. No global factorization criterion or immersion assertion for $q$ is part of this statement.

source.place: final paragraph, gluing characterized patches; Schemes Tags 01JB and 01JC

proof.text: Put q i = j i followed by the inclusion of U i in S. Restrict W i to V(i,k) = the inverse image of U k under q i. Its map to S factors both through U i and through U k. Compatibility with i,k gives a factor of the latter map through j k, hence a map V(i,k) to W k over S. Its image lies in V(k,i), so it factors through that open restriction. Reversing i,k gives the inverse: after composition into S each composite is the original structure map, and q i and q k are monomorphisms. The same cancellation proves uniqueness.

These unique isomorphisms restrict to the triple intersections and satisfy the cocycle identity, because both composites have the same map to S. The restriction maps V(i,k) to W i are open immersions. Apply scheme gluing (Tags 01JB and 01JC) to obtain Z with open charts e i from W i. The maps q i agree on the overlaps, so open-cover morphism gluing gives a map q from Z to S.

The image of e i is the inverse image of U i under q. One inclusion follows from q composed with e i = q i. For the other, choose a chart e k containing a point z whose image under q lies in U i. Its preimage in W k belongs to V(k,i), whose comparison with V(i,k) identifies z with a point in the e i chart. Thus the two open subsets coincide. Since e i and the inclusion of U i are open immersions, this equality and the commutative square give the asserted Cartesian square (the universal property of an open restriction). For empty S the point-indexed family is empty; take the empty scheme for Z and its unique map to S, and the chart assertions are vacuous.

theorem exists_gluedCompatibleImmersionCharts (S : Scheme.{u})
    (U : S → S.Opens) (hU : ∀ s : S, s ∈ U s)
    (W : S → Scheme.{u}) (j : ∀ s : S, W s ⟶ (U s).toScheme)
    (hj : ∀ s : S, IsImmersion (j s))
    (hcompat : ∀ (i k : S) {T : Scheme.{u}}
      (a : T ⟶ (U i).toScheme) (b : T ⟶ (U k).toScheme),
      a ≫ (U i).ι = b ≫ (U k).ι →
      ((∃ h : T ⟶ W i, h ≫ j i = a) ↔ (∃ h : T ⟶ W k, h ≫ j k = b))) :
    ∃ (Z : Scheme.{u}) (q : Z ⟶ S),
      ∀ i : S, ∃ e : W i ⟶ Z, IsPullback (j i) e (U i).ι q
